newsitem.title: USA: Much-needed moisture falls in Florida citrus belt.
newsitem.headline: Much-needed moisture falls in Florida citrus belt.

text.p: There were varying amounts of rain in all areas of the Florida citrus belt this week, said Florida Agricultural Statistics Service (FASS).
The much-needed moisture will greatly enhance tree condition during this all important fruit set period. There continues to be new growth on trees of all ages, it said.
Caretakers are mowing, chopping and discing cover crops. Spring herbicides are being applied in most areas to reduce weed growth under trees, FASS said.
FASS said an estimated 7,015,000 boxes of Valencia oranges were harvested in the week ended April 13, up from 6,291,000 in the prior week and compared with 5,022,000 during the week ended March 30.
There were no boxes of early and mid oranges harvested in the week ended April 13, compared to 4,000 boxes the prior week, FASS said.
